items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general municipal law, in relation to enhancing
flexibility within the county-wide shared services initiative; and to repeal
certain provisions of the general municipal law relating thereto
items.lawCode: Amd §239-bb, rpld §239-bb sub 11, Gen Muni L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6445

SPONSOR: REICHLIN-MELNICK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to enhancing
flexibility within the county-wide shared services initiative; and to
repeal certain provisions of the general municipal law relating thereto

 
PURPOSE:

To allow school districts to be part of county-wide shared services
panels.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends subdivision 2 of section 239-bb of the
general municipal law to require the participation of a school district
representative on the relevant county-wide shared services panel. The
school district representative shall be elected by majority vote of the
school board.

Section 2. of the bill amends subdivision 8 of section 239-bb of the
general municipal law, stating each county can submit one consolidated
application for matching funds for each approved and transmitted savings
plan. This section also specifies that counties will be eligible for
matching funds for savings achieved during either: (i) june 1st through
december 31 following a plan's approval or (ii) july 1st through through
june 31st following a plan's approval.

Section 3. Repeals subdivision 11 of section 239-bb of the general
municipal law. Section 4. Establishes an effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Residents of New York State carry a heavy property tax burden.  Accord-
ing to a 2019 report issued by the State Comptroller, there are over
3,700 jurisdictions across the state that possess independent authority
to levy property taxes.  Residents often pay multiple tax bills per year
because of overlapping taxing jurisdictions including county, city or
town, village, fire and other special districts in which a resident's
home is located. Together, these independent taxing authorities place a
significant financial burden on New York State residents.  The property
taxes levied by school districts across the state make=up a significant
portion of a homeowner's overall property tax burden.  According to the
Comptroller's report cited above, school districts levied $23 billion in
taxes in 2019. This amounts to 63% of total property taxes levied across
the state.

To alleviate the financial burden associated with property taxes, the
state established the "County-Wide Shared Services Initiative" in the
2018-19 budget. According to the Governor's office " 
The panel will
develop a County-Wide Shared Service Property Tax Savings Plan to iden-
tify, propose and implement new actions to save taxpayers money through
shared, coordinated and more efficient services between local govern-
ments within the county."

This bill would require that school districts located within a county
participate in the shared services panel. As it currently exists now,
the law renders their participation optional while mandating that all
other independent taxing authorities participate in the panel. While
school districts may ultimately decide that sharing services with other
governmental entities is not wise or desirable, their participation in
the countywide shared services panel would at least provide an opportu-
nity for the panel to find greater savings.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

No prior legislative history.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of July next succeeding 16 the
date on which it shall have become a law.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6445A

SPONSOR: REICHLIN-MELNICK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the general municipal law, in relation to extending the
county-wide shared services initiative and enhancing flexibility within

 
PURPOSE:

To extend the County-Wide Shared Services Initiative and to enhance
flexibility within the program.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends subdivision 8 of section 239-bb of the
General Municipal Law, stating each county can submit one consolidated
application for matching funds for each approved and transmitted savings
plan. The change to this section specifies that counties will be eligi-
ble for matching funds for savings achieved during either:

(i) January 1st through December 31 following a plan's approval or

(ii) July 1st through June 31st following a plan's approval.

Sections 2 and 3 extend the period of the program's effectiveness from
June 30, 2022 to June 30, 2025.

Section 4 provides an immediate effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Residents of New York State carry a heavy property tax burden.  Accord-
ing to a 2019 report issued by the State Comptroller, there are over
3,700 jurisdictions across the state that possess independent authority
to levy property taxes. Residents often pay multiple tax bills per year
because of overlapping taxing jurisdictions including county, city or
town, village, fire and other.special districts in which a resident's
home is located. Together, these independent taxing authorities place a
significant financial burden on New York State residents.

To alleviate the financial burden associated with property taxes, the
State established the "County-Wide Shared Services Initiative" in the
2018-19 budget. According to the Governor's office "the panel will
develop a County-Wide Shared Service Property Tax Savings Plan to iden-
tify, propose and implement new actions to save taxpayers money through
shared, coordinated and more efficient services between local govern-
ments within the county."

These changes not only extend the program, but will allow more local
governments to take advantage of the program by offering flexibility
with regard to plan implementation timelines.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

No prior legislative history.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
